topics.title: Why keyword search misses meaning

kcs.statement: Keyword matching compares strings, so it misses paraphrases and is fooled by shared words with a different intent.

problem_ideas: Find two help-centre queries that share no words with the article that answers them
Explain why “car insurance quote” misses “auto insurance quote”
Rank three articles for “cheap flights to Goa” by shared words and spot the wrong winner
Show a shared word that fools keyword ranking into the wrong intent
List three paraphrases a synonym list would miss
Decide when exact keyword match beats meaning (error codes, SKUs)

lens.reason: Every semantic-search job starts from the keyword gap.

topics.title: Describing things with numbers

kcs.statement: A vector is a list of feature values that describes a thing.
The features you choose decide what “similar” means.

serves.reason: Similarity by hand starts from feature vectors.

problem_ideas: Describe five animals with three hand-picked features and find each one's nearest neighbour
Change one feature's scale and watch the neighbours change
Explain why one-hot vectors make dog and puppy as different as dog and truck
Pick features that make two support tickets similar for routing
Count the dimensions of a feature vector for a product catalogue
Argue which of two feature sets better captures ‘similar recipes’

lens.reason: Feature vectors are the intuition every later topic leans on.

topics.title: Dot product and cosine

kcs.statement: Cosine similarity = dot product ÷ (‖a‖ ‖b‖).
Cosine lies in [−1, 1]; 0 means orthogonal.
Scaling a vector by a positive number leaves its cosine unchanged.
Compute the cosine of two small vectors by hand.

serves.reason: Computes similarity by hand and explains why cosine ignores length.

requires.reason: Cosine compares two feature vectors; without them there is nothing to compare.

problem_ideas: Compute the cosine of [1, 2, 2] and [2, 4, 4] and explain the result
Find a pair of 2-D vectors with cosine exactly 0
Show that doubling a vector leaves its cosine with any other vector unchanged
Implement cosine_sim in plain Python and test it on orthogonal and opposite vectors
Rank three short documents for a query vector by cosine by hand
Explain when cosine and dot product give different rankings

lens.reason: Cosine is the similarity every embedding stack ships with.

topics.title: What an embedding model is

kcs.statement: An embedding model maps input to a fixed-length vector so that similar meanings land close together.
Vectors are comparable only within one model.
Single dimensions of an embedding carry no readable meaning.

serves.reason: Semantic search embeds documents and queries with one model.

requires.reason: Closeness between embeddings is measured with cosine.

problem_ideas: Embed five sentences and find the two closest by cosine
Explain why a 384-dimension vector has no ‘topic’ dimension
Predict what happens when queries use model B and documents model A
Compare the length of embeddings for a word, a sentence and a paragraph
Sketch where paraphrases and unrelated sentences land on a 2-D projection
Explain an embedding to a product manager in three sentences

lens.reason: The core object of the course.

topics.title: Semantic search in four moves

kcs.statement: Embed documents offline, embed the query with the same model, rank by similarity, return the top-k.
Which steps run once and which run per query, and what each costs.

serves.reason: This is the search the course builds and evaluates.

requires.reason: Search embeds every document and every query.
Ranking scores each document by cosine.

problem_ideas: Trace a query through the four moves on the help-centre bench
Estimate per-query cost for 10k documents with exact ranking
Decide which step must be redone when an article changes
Predict the top-3 for a query given a small similarity table
Find the bug when queries are embedded with a different model
Explain why top-k is cut after ranking, not before

lens.reason: The pipeline every later unit improves.

topics.title: Learning by contrast

kcs.statement: Contrastive training pulls matching pairs together and pushes in-batch negatives apart.
“Similar” means whatever the training pairs said was similar.

requires.reason: Explains how an embedding model learned to place meanings.

problem_ideas: Draw one contrastive step for a batch of three pairs
Explain why in-batch negatives make large batches better
Predict which pair a QA-trained model scores higher: paraphrase or answer
Choose training pairs for a duplicate-ticket detector
Explain why ‘similar’ is not ‘relevant’ for a search engine
Spot the leakage when test queries appear in training pairs

lens.reason: Knowing what the model was trained on explains its failures on the job.

topics.title: Pooling and token limits

kcs.statement: Token vectors are pooled into one vector for the whole input.
Input past the model's max length is truncated, silently in some libraries.

serves.reason: Truncation decides what a document vector actually contains.

requires.reason: Pooling is the last step inside an embedding model.

problem_ideas: Mean-pool three token vectors by hand
Find the sentence a 256-token model never sees in a long article
Explain why mean pooling blurs a long document's topics
Check a library's max_seq_length and what it does past it
Predict the effect of moving the answer to the end of a long document
Compare CLS pooling with mean pooling on one example

lens.reason: Silent truncation is a top cause of bad retrieval.

topics.title: Metrics and normalisation

kcs.statement: For unit vectors, cosine, dot product and Euclidean distance give identical rankings.
An unnormalised dot product favours long vectors.

serves.reason: Choosing the metric correctly is part of a working search.

requires.reason: Compares cosine with dot product and Euclidean distance.

problem_ideas: Normalise two vectors and check that dot product equals cosine
Rank three vectors by dot, cosine and Euclidean and compare
Show a long vector winning on dot product but not on cosine
Choose the FAISS metric for normalised embeddings
Derive ‖a − b‖² = 2 − 2cos for unit vectors
Debug a search where long articles always rank first

lens.reason: Index settings ask for the metric on day one.

topics.title: Choosing a model

kcs.statement: Choose an embedding model by language and domain, max input, dimensions and cost.
Decide with an eval on your own queries, not a leaderboard alone.
Respect query and document prefixes, and never mix models in one index.

serves.reason: Chooses a model under stated constraints.

requires.reason: Choosing compares embedding models.
Max input length is a selection criterion.

problem_ideas: Shortlist two models for Hindi support tickets and justify each
Design a 30-query eval to choose between two models
Estimate storage for 1M docs at 384 vs 1536 dimensions
Find the bug when an E5 model is used without its query prefix
Decide whether a bigger model is worth 4× the cost
Plan the switch from model A to model B without mixing vectors

lens.reason: Model choice is a weekly decision on the job.

topics.title: Chunking

kcs.statement: Chunks that are too big dilute meaning; chunks that are too small lose context.
Overlap and context headers recover context lost at chunk boundaries.

serves.reason: Chunking decides what a search can return.

requires.reason: Chunking exists because inputs are pooled and truncated.

problem_ideas: Chunk an article at 50 and 200 words and compare which query finds the answer
Add 20% overlap and show the boundary answer becoming retrievable
Write a context header for a chunk from a FAQ section
Predict recall when chunks are a whole page each
Pick a chunk size for a 256-token model
Explain why chunking by heading beats fixed windows for docs

lens.reason: Chunking is the first knob tuned in every RAG system.

topics.title: Measuring retrieval: recall@k, MRR, nDCG

kcs.statement: Retrieval quality is measured on labelled queries.
Compute recall@k and precision@k for a ranked list.
Compute MRR; nDCG weights graded relevance by rank.

requires.reason: Evaluates a search pipeline's ranked output.

problem_ideas: Compute recall@5 and precision@5 for one ranked list
Compute MRR over three queries by hand
Implement recall_at_k and mrr and test them on edge cases
Explain why nDCG needs graded labels
Label 10 queries for the help-centre bench
Decide which metric to report for a single-answer FAQ

lens.reason: Without an eval, every change is a guess.

topics.title: Why exact search stops scaling

kcs.statement: Exact search costs N·d per query; ANN indexes trade a little recall for large speedups, measured against an exact baseline.

serves.reason: Chooses an index under a latency constraint.

requires.reason: Exact search ranks every document for every query.

problem_ideas: Compute multiply-adds per query for 10M × 768
Estimate exact-search latency on one CPU core
Decide at which corpus size exact search stops meeting 50 ms
Explain what ‘recall against exact’ measures
Predict how latency grows when the corpus doubles
Name two ways to cut exact cost without ANN

topics.title: IVF: partition, then probe

kcs.statement: IVF puts vectors into k-means cells and scans only the nprobe nearest cells.
Border neighbours can be missed; nprobe trades latency for recall.

requires.reason: IVF answers the cost of exact search.

problem_ideas: Assign six 2-D points to two k-means cells by hand
Find the query whose true neighbour sits in the next cell
Predict recall at nprobe 1, 2 and 4
Estimate vectors scanned per query for 1M vectors in 1,000 cells
Choose nlist for 10M vectors
Explain why IVF needs training data and HNSW does not

lens.reason: IVF is common in FAISS and pgvector deployments.

topics.title: HNSW

kcs.statement: HNSW runs a greedy beam search over a layered proximity graph.
M and efConstruction trade memory and build time for recall.
efSearch is the query-time recall and latency knob.

requires.reason: HNSW answers the cost of exact search.

problem_ideas: Trace a greedy search on a 10-node graph
Predict recall at efSearch 10 and 100
Estimate link memory for M = 16 and 10M vectors
Tune efSearch to recall@10 ≥ 0.95 of exact
Explain why the top layer has so few nodes
Choose between IVF and HNSW for a corpus that changes hourly

lens.reason: HNSW is the default index in most vector stores.

topics.title: Quantisation and shorter embeddings

kcs.statement: float16, int8, binary and product quantisation shrink memory at some recall cost.
Oversample-and-rescore and shorter Matryoshka vectors recover recall or trade size.

requires.reason: Compression attacks the memory side of exact search.

problem_ideas: Compute RAM for 10M × 768 at float32, int8 and binary
Predict recall after binary quantisation with and without rescoring
Truncate a Matryoshka vector to 256 dimensions and compare rankings
Choose a compression for a 100M-vector index on one machine
Explain product quantisation with two sub-vectors
Decide how much to oversample before rescoring

lens.reason: Useful past ~10M vectors; most jobs start smaller.

topics.title: Hybrid search, RRF and reranking

kcs.statement: Hybrid search fuses BM25 and vector results by rank.
RRF score = Σ 1 ÷ (k + rank).
Cross-encoders rerank the top candidates for precision.

serves.reason: Chooses a hybrid and reranking setup under constraints.

requires.reason: Hybrid search keeps keyword matching for the exact terms vectors blur.
Fusion combines the vector result list.
Whether fusion helps is judged with recall@k.

problem_ideas: Fuse two ranked lists with RRF at k = 60 by hand
Find the error-code query BM25 wins and vectors lose
Predict how k changes the fused order
Decide how many candidates to send to a cross-encoder
Measure recall@10 before and after hybrid on the bench
Explain why score averaging fails across BM25 and cosine

lens.reason: Hybrid plus rerank is the production default.

topics.title: Production pitfalls

kcs.statement: Model migrations need full re-embedding, and stored vectors go stale.
Post-filtering after ANN search can starve the results.
Similarity thresholds are model-specific; never borrow one.

serves.reason: Diagnoses the production failures the course names.

requires.reason: A model change forces re-embedding.
Truncation and chunking failures surface in production.
Filter starvation happens after ANN search.

problem_ideas: Diagnose a search that returns 2 results when 10 were asked for with a filter
Plan a zero-downtime re-embedding after a model upgrade
Recalibrate a duplicate threshold for a new model
Find the stale vectors after an article edit
Explain why mixing two models' vectors breaks ranking
Write a monitoring check that catches truncation in production

lens.reason: These are the incidents a job will page you for.
